## Q10 - Question 6: Must a type law be proven before it can be used?

I think we have now reached the most consequential unresolved design choice.

Suppose Jev reconstructs the entire musical alignment and discovers a new candidate operator or type relationship that resolves several major discrepancies.

It has not yet produced an independently confirmed prediction, but the relationship is internally lawful and provides several new testable consequences.

Should SUNNY be allowed to immediately use that candidate relationship to derive further possibilities, while keeping its authority conditional?

My proposed answer is **yes**\.

This would give SUNNY a system in which emerging types can be used provisionally without being prematurely locked into the architecture. Their consequences can be explored, compared, and tested in parallel.
